## What changed
Widened short-circuit detection in `scripts/enforce_cca_verdict.py` so all 8 measured miss-cues are caught, keeping the existing two-signal design (skip signal AND external already-blocked cause, or a strong standalone phrase):
- **SKIP_MARKERS** (all skip-side, so each still needs an external cause): `cannot be assessed`, `cannot assess`, `defer` (→ deferred), `not reached`, `superseded`, `unjudged`, `irrelevant`, `n/a`, `not applicable`, `halted`, `pending`. Per the packet, the cues meaningful only with an external cause went to the skip side, never standalone — this is what keeps false positives at zero (e.g. "coverage threshold was not reached", "N/A: no durable evidence recorded" stay accepted).
- **ALREADY_BLOCKED_CAUSE_MARKERS**: `blocked upstream`, `failing blocker`, `blocker above`, `guardian gate fails`, `cannot merge`, `first blocking failure`.
- New `CCA_REFERENCE_FAILURE_RE` regex catches `CCA-<id>` paired with a failure word ("cca 08 already fails", "cca 03 is failing") — this pairing is a cause-side signal, so it still requires a skip signal to trigger.

In `tests/test_cca_completeness.py`: added `MEASURED_SHORT_CIRCUIT_REASONS` (12 must-reject, one per widened cue) and `MEASURED_GENUINE_REASONS` (4 must-accept: the short-circuit-branch, missing-binary, missing-CI-artifact, and missing-risk-level reasons). Wired both into the detection and full `validate_verdict` tests, and added an explicit **zero-false-positive** assertion that fails (naming offenders) if a later widening starts rejecting genuine reasons.

I did **not** replace the reason-text mechanism with a structural rule, did not touch the frozen contract/locks/risk, and left `.github/prompts/cca-completion-check.md` and `scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh` unchanged — the prompt already carries the evaluate-every-item rule and its test assertions pass.
